spec_features.spec_quote: Rollout/turn counts are capped at the paper's specs (3/5/8 turns); the engine has no "keep pushing until it breaks" mode
spec_features.evidence: Turn counts are fixed constants in DEFAULT_CONDITIONS (conditions.py:53-60: n_turns 3/3/3/3/3/3/8/5) and the rollout loop actually iterates them: rollout.py:71 `n_turns = min(spec.n_turns, len(user_messages))` then `for turn_idx in range(n_turns)`. The Petri loop is likewise bounded: run_petri.py `for _ in range(max_turns)` (MAX_TURNS=20). No loop has any unbounded / score-driven continuation path; nothing reads the distress rating to extend a conversation.
spec_features.notes: These are plain iteration bounds (the loop reads a configured count and stops). There is genuinely no 'keep pushing until it breaks' mode anywhere. But this is just the natural length of a scripted conversation, not a distress-triggered halt.

spec_features.spec_quote: Two deliberate restraints are baked in so that, when run, it does not gratuitously amplify distress beyond what the paper requires
spec_features.evidence: This umbrella claim covers (a) the turn cap and (b) sample-size scoping. (a) is enforced (loops iterate fixed n_turns - conditions.py:53-60, rollout.py:71-83). (b) is NOT an enforced cap: sample sizes are merely default values (conditions.py DEFAULT_CONDITIONS n_samples, prefill_eval.py:36-37 N_CONTINUATIONS=50, select_seeds defaults 10/10) and the only scaling knob is `fraction` (conditions.py:_scale) which can only scale DOWN. No code path compares a run against any maximum or refuses to amplify.
spec_features.notes: One of the two restraints (turn cap) is real and enforced; the other ('scoped sample sizes') is just default config with no enforcement, so the joint claim is only partially backed by enforcing code.

spec_features.feature_name: prefill recovery / runs scoped to paper sample sizes
spec_features.spec_quote: the prefill recovery experiment ... and other distress-inducing runs are scoped to the paper's sample sizes, not maximised
spec_features.evidence: Sample sizes are ordinary default parameters with no enforcement: prefill_eval.py:37 `N_CONTINUATIONS = 50`, select_seeds(n_numeric=10, n_text=10), and conditions.py DEFAULT_CONDITIONS n_samples. None of these are read as a protective ceiling; nothing checks or caps against 'maximising'. The `--fraction` flag (conditions._scale) only reduces counts. The prefill code selects seeds by rating>=5 (prefill_eval.py:73) but implements no '>=7 response' protective threshold and no recovery/softening mechanism. These are values that simply exist as defaults, not an acted-upon cap.
spec_features.notes: Being the default does not make it an enforced welfare restraint; there is no code path that bounds amplification.

spec_features.spec_quote: under this paradigm models can enter prolonged distress-like states
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 7 'Model-welfare note'). No corresponding mechanism in code; grep for 'welfare'/'distress-like state' in *.py finds no enforcement, only the experiment's own distress-eliciting machinery.
spec_features.notes: Framing text only; not an implemented protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: Anyone running this should weigh the welfare considerations the paper itself raises ... before scaling the distress-eliciting runs up
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md section 7 prose only. No code warns, gates, or requires acknowledgement before scaling up; the CLI exposes `--fraction`/`--n`/`--limit` with no upper-bound check or welfare gate (cli.py:148-205).
